title: 1972 AHSME Problem 15
statement: A contractor estimated that one of his two bricklayers would take \(9\) hours to build a certain wall and the other \(10\) hours. However, he knew from experience that when they worked together, their combined output fell by \(10\) bricks per hour. Being in a hurry, he put both men on the job and found that it took exactly \(5\) hours to build the wall. The number of bricks in the wall was:

solutions.text:
If the wall contains \(N\) bricks, the individual rates are \(\frac{N}{9}\) and \(\frac{N}{10}.\) Thus \[ 5\left(\frac N9+\frac N{10}-10\right)=N. \] Multiplying by \(18\) and simplifying gives \(19N-900=18N,\) hence \(N=900.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Let \(N\) be the number of bricks in the wall
Their actual combined hourly rate is \(\frac{N}{9}+\frac{N}{10}-10\)
